source: Minchat Shai on Torah, Gen 1:11 (Shivrei Luchot; precise books)
claim_en: tadshe ('let the earth sprout') is written with a meteg (the small stress-stroke) — the Masorah note the Shivrei Luchot records, and the reading of the precise books.

source: Minchat Shai on Torah, Gen 1:11 (books divided; Et Sofer prefers revia)
claim_en: deshe ('sprout', the command's first product-word) — MS records the books DIVIDED: some read zaqef qatan (the small two-dot pause), the Sephardic books and the early print read revia, and Radak's Et Sofer rules for revia. SNAPSHOT carries the zaqef qatan — joining the camp MS argues against (split-attested accent station).

source: Minchat Shai on Torah, Gen 1:11 (the Michlol)
claim_en: In the command's fruit-clause the pe of peri ('fruit') after ose ('making') takes a dagesh (the hardening dot) by the approaching-from-afar rule (ati merachik) — first of the pair MS cites from the Michlol.

source: Minchat Shai on Torah, Gen 1:11 (the Michlol)
claim_en: In the delivery the pe of peri again takes the dagesh — this time by the crowded-word rule (dechik), 'for it stands with a maqqef (the joining stroke)': second of the Michlol pair.

source: Minchat Shai on Torah, Gen 1:11 (the Michlol)
claim_en: The dechik driver itself: ose ('making') at the delivery IS joined to peri by maqqef (the joining stroke) — while the command's ose at 1:11 stands unjoined, exactly the split the two Michlol rules require.

source: Minchat Shai on Torah, Gen 1:11 (manuscripts, early print, Et Sofer)
claim_en: zar-o ('its seed') is joined to vo ('in it') by maqqef, without a meteg — first of the two stations MS rules 'both with maqqef'.

source: Minchat Shai on Torah, Gen 1:11 (manuscripts, early print, Et Sofer)
claim_en: The second station of the pair: zar-o ('its seed') joined to vo ('in it') by maqqef in the delivery verse too.
mazria zera le-minehu ('yielding seed after its kind') — the three initials spell mazal ('constellation'): no blade of grass without a constellation above it.

etz peri ('fruit-tree' — tree whose taste is its fruit) as an adjacent bare pair stands ONCE in the Torah, in the command; the delivery gives etz ose peri ('tree MAKING fruit') and the commanded phrase never returns — the spec/delivery delta the earth was cursed for.
In the command the kind-word appears ONCE — le-min-o ('after its kind') on the tree only; the grasses were never commanded it.
In the delivery the kind-word appears TWICE — le-mine-hu on the grasses (who reasoned it out a fortiori) and on the tree: the grasses' own addition, honored in the ledger.
